newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: FOCUS-Jobs group Adecco aims to grow margins.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Jobs group Adecco aims to grow margins.

text.p: Europe's largest job recruitment group Adecco SA said on Wednesday it planned to improve its margins, partly by cutting costs, following the merger last year of Swiss-based Adia and France's Ecco.
"The challenge is for us to become more and more cost-efficient," John Bowmer, Adecco's chief executive officer said during a presention on the company's 1996 results.

Taking the merger into account, which involved Adia buying Ecco shares and replacing them with Adia capital under the name Adecco, it showed an 11.1 million Swiss franc ($7.7 million) net loss. That included amortisation of goodwill worth 191.8 million Swiss francs and restructuring costs of 21.3 million.
Pro forma net income before goodwill amortisation was 241 million Swiss francs in 1996 versus 206 million in 1995. Adecco said it would pay a 5.00 Swiss franc dividend on its 1996 results.

Operating income as a percent of revenue fell to 4.6 percent from 4.7 percent, although operating income in absolute terms rose to 387.9 million Swiss francs from 355.7 million. Pro forma revenue rose 12 percent to 8.524 billion francs from 7.609 billion in 1995.
Bowmer said Adecco's internal target was for earnings before interest and taxation (EBIT) of 5.0 percent of revenue.
"We see the way forward in investing in technology, so we become the lowest-cost producer."

Bowmer said the cost of developing and implementing technological improvements was still being asessed. The company expects to have a major study on its strategy for the next five years completed at the end of April.

Bowmer said Adecco is now "one of the two truly global companies" in the personnel services market, which he estimated was worth $100 billion worldwide. It is rivaled in size only by U.S.-based Manpower Inc.

In France, which produces nearly half of Adecco's revenues, Bowmer said both Adecco and Manpower had gained market share in the past year. He said the market would remain a battle but the trend favoured larger, cost-effective providers.

Adecco's activities range from mainstream brokering of temporary positions, where margins have come under pressure, to providing specialists in areas like technology where margins are helped by shortages of qualified specialists.
Adecco's contract, or multinational business also saw some pressure on margins due to increasing competition.
The company was optimistic for 1997, saying its French business had picked up in the first two months of this year, showing volume increases of 10 to 12 percent.
Adecco said it would like to increase its market share in the United States, which comprises roughly half the worldwide market,.
It is not ruling out further acquisitions. It is still waiting for deregulation in Italy, while German and Japanese regulations impose limitations although rules are changing.
Adecco expects to open around 100 branches, and about 100 "on-site" personnel offices at major clients this year. It currently has about 2,500 offices worldwide.

Its shares are listed on the Swiss electronic stock exchange, and on the Paris stock exchange. Its Swiss listed shares rose six francs to a high of 456 Swiss francs before edging back to 455 by 1215 GMT
